questions.prompt: A useState call runs only when showDetails is true. What is the repair?

choices.text: Call useState unconditionally at the component top level.
Call useState after an early return for showDetails false.
Place useState inside a loop with one conditional iteration.
Call useState from the click handler that toggles showDetails.

questions.explanation: Ordinary Hook call order must stay stable. Put the call before conditional returns and condition the UI instead.

sources.title: Rules of Hooks
sources.claim: Ordinary Hooks such as useState and useEffect must be called at the top level of React components or custom Hooks, not in conditions, loops or event handlers.

questions.prompt: Which location can directly call useEffect?

choices.text: The top level of a React component or custom Hook.
A plain utility function called only after a network response.
A conditional branch skipped by the first component render.
A button click callback after the component has committed.

questions.explanation: React components and custom Hooks are allowed callers; arbitrary callbacks and conditional locations are not.

sources.title: Rules of Hooks

questions.prompt: Two components call the same useDraft custom Hook. What is shared automatically?

choices.text: The Hook code, while each call retains its own local state.
One synchronized draft, because each caller passes the same arguments.
One draft value, because all calls use the same function.
One component identity across both caller tree positions.

questions.explanation: Extracting a Hook shares implementation logic, not one state instance. Shared state requires another mechanism.

sources.title: Reusing Logic with Custom Hooks
sources.claim: Custom Hooks share stateful logic, not state itself; each call is independent, can accept reactive values and should be named use followed by a capital letter.

questions.prompt: A helper calls useState and useEffect. Why name it useConnection?

choices.text: The prefix allows conditional Hook calls in event handlers.
The prefix marks it as a custom Hook subject to Hook rules.
The prefix turns it into a component that must return JSX.
The prefix makes all its invocations share one global connection.

questions.explanation: The naming convention makes Hook behavior visible and lintable. It does not waive ordering rules or share state.

sources.title: Reusing Logic with Custom Hooks
sources.claim: Custom Hooks share stateful logic, not state itself; each call is independent, can accept reactive values and should be named use followed by a capital letter.

questions.prompt: State is {address: {city: "A"}}. Which update preserves immutable history?

choices.text: Assign a new city property on a module variable without a setter.
Mutate state.address.city, then pass the original state object.
Spread only state, then mutate the shared address object.
Copy state and address, setting city on the new address object.

questions.explanation: Spread is shallow. Both the outer object and the modified nested address need fresh identities.

sources.title: Updating Objects in State
sources.claim: React state should be treated as read-only; object spread is shallow, so nested updates copy each changed level, and setting a new object requests a render.

questions.prompt: An event mutates user.name directly without calling the setter. Why may the displayed name remain old?

choices.text: React updates the DOM immediately before the event handler returns.
Every state object is automatically frozen in all production apps.
React tracks each property assignment through a state proxy.
Mutation alone does not request a render and alters old snapshots.

questions.explanation: Treat state as read-only and request an update with a new value. Mutation is neither notification nor snapshot preservation.

questions.prompt: Which ordinary Hook usages follow the Rules of Hooks? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Call useState inside a custom Hook invoked at the top level.
Ordinary Hooks may run after an early return if the condition was false initially.
Call useEffect only inside an if branch that sometimes runs.
Call useState unconditionally before early returns.
Call useState from a click callback after the render completes.

questions.explanation: A: Correct: custom Hooks are allowed callers. B: Incorrect: Hook order must remain consistent across renders. C: Incorrect: conditional calls can change order. D: Correct: this keeps Hook order stable. E: Incorrect: callbacks are not component rendering or Hook execution.

sources.claim: Ordinary Hook calls follow top-level order in components and custom Hooks; eslint-plugin-react-hooks detects violations.

questions.prompt: Which custom-Hook statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A custom Hook must return a JSX element like a component.
Extracting a Hook can remove duplicated stateful behavior code.
Reactive arguments can change what a custom Hook synchronizes.
Separate invocations can each have independent local state.
Every call to one custom Hook shares one state object automatically.

questions.explanation: A: Incorrect: Hooks may return arbitrary values. B: Correct: Hooks reuse behavior implementation. C: Correct: Hook code reruns with current arguments. D: Correct: state is isolated for each invocation. E: Incorrect: calls have independent state.

sources.title: Reusing Logic with Custom Hooks
sources.claim: Custom Hooks share logic rather than state, may return arbitrary values and receive reactive arguments.

questions.prompt: Which claims explain shallow object copying? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Changing a nested field requires copying the changed path.
Mutating the shared nested object leaves the original snapshot unchanged.
Object spread creates a new outer object.
An unchanged nested object can remain shared by both copies.
Object spread recursively clones every nested object by default.

questions.explanation: A: Correct: copy each modified level. B: Incorrect: shared nested mutation alters both references. C: Correct: the outer identity is new. D: Correct: unchanged nested references can be reused. E: Incorrect: object spread is shallow.

questions.prompt: Which practices support reliable React state updates? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Keep old nested objects unchanged when producing an updated state.
Pass a newly constructed updated object to the setter.
Mutate an old state object to notify React without its setter.
Treat existing state objects as read-only snapshots.
Assume setter calls retroactively rewrite all previous render snapshots.

questions.explanation: A: Correct: immutable updates preserve earlier snapshots. B: Correct: this queues the new state. C: Incorrect: mutation is not an update signal. D: Correct: snapshots should remain stable. E: Incorrect: existing snapshots retain their old values.
